passage:
At the play centre, Jaya saw the red truck roll past and grabbed it straight out of another child's hands. The child wailed. Jaya clutched the truck and ran behind the book shelf.
Uma, the teacher, crouched beside her. "Jaya, your hands were very fast." Jaya's lip wobbled.
Uma held up her palm. "Stop hand first. Then words: 'Can I have a turn?'"
Jaya looked at the truck, then at the crying child, and slowly pushed it back across the floor.
Later she wanted the blocks. Her hand shot out, then froze in mid-air. "Turn?" she whispered.

qa.q: Where did Jaya run with the truck?
qa.a: Behind the book shelf.

qa.q: Why did Jaya grab the truck without asking?
qa.a: Jaya felt eager for the truck the moment she saw it, and the grab came before any thought about the other child.

qa.q: What did Uma teach that suits a fast-acting child?
qa.a: A simple 'stop hand' first, then words, a short pause Jaya can actually use.

qa.q: How might the other child have felt when the truck came back?
qa.a: Relieved and calmer, though maybe still a bit wary of Jaya's fast hands.

grounding: A preschooler grabs a toy and runs on impulse, then begins to learn a brief pause with a teacher's stop-hand signal.

passage:
I'm Vidya, Raghav's Masi, and I took him to the colony park for an hour.
His ball bounced toward the gate. Raghav shot after it without a glance at the road. I was running before I'd thought either. I caught his collar just as a scooter went past.
He wriggled, furious, and smacked my arm. "My ball!"
I held him until his breathing slowed. I can't know what was in his head, but it didn't look like thinking. Ball, run. Masi, hit.
Afterwards we practised: ball goes out, feet freeze, shout for Masi. By the fourth try he froze like a statue, grinning.

qa.q: What went past the gate as Vidya caught Raghav's collar?
qa.a: A scooter.

qa.q: Why did Raghav smack Vidya's arm?
qa.a: He was furious at being stopped from getting his ball, and the anger came out as a hit before he could think.

qa.q: Why is the freeze game a good fit for Raghav?
qa.a: It gives him one simple action to practise, feet freeze and shout, so the pause can become a habit before his body runs.

qa.q: What was that moment like for Vidya?
qa.a: Frightening: she ran without thinking too, and then had to stay calm while he hit and wriggled.

grounding: An aunt watches a preschooler dash after a ball toward the road and hit when stopped, acting on impulse with no pause.

passage:
Monday. Little Jatin knocked over Amandeep's block tower. Amandeep's hand flew out and whacked Jatin's head before anyone could blink. Jatin howled.
Wednesday. Mama sat with Amandeep on the rug. "When you feel the hot hand, squeeze it into a ball, tight, tight. Then shout for me." They practised squeezing and shouting, giggling.
Saturday. Jatin crawled straight into the new tower. Crash. Amandeep's arm went up, and stopped. His fist squeezed shut, shaking. "MAMA! He broke it!"
Mama came running and hugged him. "You squeezed! I saw it."
Amandeep scowled at the blocks, then started building again.

qa.q: What did Jatin do on Saturday?
qa.a: He crawled straight into the new tower.

qa.q: What does Amandeep's shaking fist on Saturday suggest?
qa.a: He was still very angry, but the practised squeeze gave him a moment to hold back instead of hitting.

qa.q: What made Mama's plan work?
qa.a: It gave Amandeep something to do with the 'hot hand' and was practised while calm, so the pause was ready when the anger came.

qa.q: How might Jatin's week look from his side?
qa.a: On Monday he got hurt over a game he didn't understand; by Saturday his brother shouted instead of hitting, which is much safer for him.

grounding: Across a week, a preschooler who hits on first impulse starts to pause with a practised fist squeeze.

passage: The wedding hall was loud and crowded, and Pradeep Chacha was holding a plate in each hand. Siddharth, four, saw the balloon arch across the room. He ran. Straight through the line of waiters carrying steaming trays. A tray tipped; rice scattered. Pradeep Chacha dropped both plates and caught Siddharth's arm. Siddharth wriggled free, grabbed a laddoo from a stranger's plate, and stuffed it in his mouth. Pradeep Chacha crouched down, breathing hard. "Siddharth. Stop. Look at me." Siddharth stopped, cheeks full, eyes wide, as if he had just noticed the waiters.

qa.q: What did Siddharth see across the room?
qa.a: The balloon arch.

qa.q: Why did Siddharth run through the waiters without stopping?
qa.a: Siddharth was so excited about the balloons that he acted on the wish at once, without any pause to notice the trays or the danger.

qa.q: What could Pradeep Chacha do to help Siddharth pause next time?
qa.a: Before entering a busy place, he could hold Siddharth's hand and practise a simple "stop and look" game together.

qa.q: How might the waiter feel when the tray tipped?
qa.a: The waiter might feel startled and frustrated, having worked to carry hot food through a crowd.

grounding: At a busy wedding, a preschooler runs and grabs on the first impulse, with little pause to think.

passage: In the colony courtyard in Hyderabad, Ritu, five, was drawing a sun with yellow chalk when Zubin took the piece right out of her hand. Ritu's hand shot out and smacked his arm. Zubin wailed. Ritu's mother knelt beside her. "Hands down first. Then words." Ritu scowled, then mumbled, "Mine." Mother gave the chalk back and said, "Zubin, ask next time." The next evening, Zubin reached for her blue chalk. Ritu's hand came up fast, and then, for one tiny second, it stopped in the air. "MINE," she shouted instead. It was not polite, but it was words.

qa.q: What was Ritu drawing with the yellow chalk?
qa.a: A sun.

qa.q: Why did Ritu smack Zubin's arm so quickly?
qa.a: She was angry that her chalk was taken, and at five she acted on that first feeling before any thought could catch up.

qa.q: What did Ritu's mother teach her, and how could she keep practising it?
qa.a: "Hands down first. Then words"; she can keep reminding Ritu gently each time and praise her when words come instead of hands.

qa.q: What was it like for Zubin when Ritu shouted instead of hitting?
qa.a: Zubin still didn't get the chalk, but was spared a smack, so the second evening was less painful for him.

grounding: A preschooler hits on impulse, then shows the first tiny pause of slower thinking the next day.
